title: Exclusive Array1/Array2 initialization ownership transition for non-Copy payloads

baseline.diagnostic: Both previous assume_init methods reject String because String: Copy is not satisfied. The new exclusive transition compiles and destroys non-Copy owned values exactly once.
baseline.lifetime_diagnostics: Both Array1 and Array2 borrowed transitions reject attempted returns with a static lifetime.

ownership_policy.Owned: Transfers the complete Vec length, capacity, pointer and allocation layout without copying, constructing or dropping elements. Result owns every actual initialized slot.
ownership_policy.Borrowed: Reinterprets only the exclusive slice, preserving length, pointer and lifetime. Dropping the result does not drop donor payloads; donor must later move or destroy each initialized slot.
ownership_policy.Shared: Always returns Err with original storage, metadata, pointer and detach function, including empty shared views. No slot is read, so rejected shared backing may be uninitialized.
ownership_policy.Array2: Carries every rectangle and base lower-bound field unchanged on both outcomes; initialization covers actual flat backing even when its length is zero, shortened or extended relative to rows times columns.
ownership_policy.Existing_Copy_transition: Original Copy-bound assume_init keeps shared view support; its exclusive cases share the new conversion engine.

native_dependency_regression.note: Inherited raw construction rows rerun unchanged; they do not create a native declaration for this Rust ownership transition. Linked TKernel binary is not fully instrumented.

remaining_limits: Unsafe callers must initialize every actual exclusive backing slot before transition; initialization is not dynamically checked.
Partial raw construction failure requires explicit prefix recovery or completion before this transition; it cannot safely convert a partially initialized array.
Shared non-Copy extraction/detachment and native writable alias protocols are not introduced.
Raw placement construction address/failing-byte effects, native constructor-failure allocation leaks and allocator hooks remain open.
No native assume_init method is invented, and no API parity credit is assigned.
